New series from The Observer with @Yoshua_Bengio, me, and others on potential catastrophic risks in AI.  

(link at bottom of thread)


Jamie Bartlett 🇬🇧 (@JamieJBartlett)

For the last few months I’ve been investigating how concerned we should be about potentially catastrophic – even existential – risks from Artificial Intelligence. It’s a 3-part podcast for The Observer. The final episode is now out.
1/

CAISI has reportedly been directed to stop publishing public model assessments as the new AI EO gets implemented.

Natsec engagement on AI is essential. But pulling CAISI's evals from public view doesn't make the field more secure. It just means fewer eyes on the science when we need more.

Openness and natsec don't have to be in tension here. We should be doing both.

I argued, publicly, AGAINST each of these foolish predictions– and got endless shit for it.

Moral: on X, you probably shouldn’t trust the “wisdom” of the crowds.


Nalin (@nalinrajput23)

Remember all the AI predictions people were making in 2024?  

"GPT-5 will be AGI" 
"Sora will replace Hollywood" 
"Devin will replace every developer by 2025" 
"Apple's AI will change everything"  

Funny how none of that actually happened.
